newsitem.title: USA: Apple shares jump 5 percent on Jobs speculation.
newsitem.headline: Apple shares jump 5 percent on Jobs speculation.

text.p: Apple Computer Inc. stock jumped 5 percent Wednesday amid speculation that Steve Jobs, the company's charismatic co-founder, would be named chairman shortly.
Shares of Apple, based in Cupertino, Calif., rose 87.5 cents to $17.375. Earlier, the shares traded as high as $17.688.

Several news organisations -- including the San Francisco Chronicle, CNBC, San Jose Mercury News and Macworld -- have reported in the past few days that Apple plans to announce Jobs' appointment as chairman at next week's Macworld trade show in Boston. Apple ousted Gilbert Amelio as chairman and chief executive three weeks ago.

If the speculation turns out to be true, Apple would be hoping to tap Jobs' enormous popularity among Macintosh fans to revive the Apple brand and get sales at the struggling company going again, analysts said.

As chairman, Jobs would be responsible for setting the company's technology and marketing strategies. Apple likely would name someone else as chief executive to handle day-to-day management, which also would let Jobs keep his roles as chairman and CEO at animation firm Pixar Animation Studios, analysts said.

Apple spokeswoman Katie Cotton said the speculation is a "rumor and we absolutely will not comment on rumours." But she would not say that the rumours are false. She confirmed that Jobs will be the keynote speaker at Macworld.
Jobs could not be reached for comment.

If he is named chairman, Jobs would return to Apple 12 years after being forced out by the board of directors and then-CEO John Sculley. He reconnected with Apple in December when Apple bought Next Software Inc., the company Jobs founded after he left Apple. Amelio brought on Jobs as part-time advisor.

"I'm glad that he would not be running day-to-day stuff, but planning long-term strategy," said Stephen Prey, vice president of the Caltrans Mac User Group, which helps several thousand Apple Macintosh users within the California transportation department. "That's where his strength is."
But it could also pose a problem for Apple in attracting a top-tier CEO to work under Jobs, analysts said. Jobs is infamous for a quick temper and an overbearing charm.

"I don't think it makes a lot of sense," said William Milton, analyst at investment bank Brown Brothers Harriman. "What kind of a CEO would Apple attract to work under Jobs? It would not be a strong leader."

Still, Apple needs a "marketing genius" to turn around plunging sales and market share, ousted chairman Amelio said yesterday in his first public speech since his resignation. Jobs would fit that bill.
While still in his early 20s, Jobs took the ingenious electronics kit that his pal Steve Wozniak whipped together in his garage in the late 1970s, and built Apple Computer.
Jobs was not available to comment on the reports but as recently as last week he was telling analysts he had no plans to become chairman of Apple.

CNBC, quoting sources familar with the company, said Apple's board of directors had signed off on the decision to hire Jobs. However, the television network said the move may be temporary until Apple finds a new chief executive, a process that could take several months.
Meanwhile, industry experts say if Jobs were to move into the top spot at Apple, his current company, Pixar Animation Studios would continue to turn out successful films.

"I don't think Pixar is dependent on Steve Jobs to be very successful at creating animated feature films that have high commercial potential," said entertainment analyst Jeffrey Logsdon at Cruttendon Roth.
